commit.message:
Add new standalone GN args and test specs

Adds the necessary new code to support Dawn-side GN args and test specs
for the upcoming Dawn standalone builders which use the gn_v2 recipe.

Additionally, adds the GN args and test specs used by the
Linux/Swiftshader configuration to act as an example and make future
testing via led easier. This does NOT actually create the builders yet,
as they are not added to //infra/config/global/main.star yet.

Bug: 385317083

the ones we require which are any which don't have an initializer.

Moves doing math on indices or using std::end instead of doing math on
pointers directly.

Also cleans up `at()` to not return a reference to a local variable,

commit.subject: Allow changing Vulkan allocator heap block size
commit.message:
Allow changing Vulkan allocator heap block size

ResourceMemoryAllocator was defaulting to a 8mb block size. That's
significantly different than VMA heap block size of 64kb used by VMA
with Ganesh/Vulkan. Graphite/Dawn/Vulkan wants to configure this
similarly so add a chainable struct wgpu::DawnAllocatorDescriptor that
configures the heap block size.

Bug: 407730048
Change-Id: Ib08f1010bf7be2014d8859631bd0848f79b49f98

commit.subject: Fix Windows build on GitHub CI
commit.message:
Fix Windows build on GitHub CI

Commit 54ad6448697e6c6da09eceabfae93f1c234bbc0e removed a test because the required version of Windows SDK to build Dawn is 22621. However, GitHub Action Windows runner uses SDK version 20348 by default.

This PR uses [fbactions/setup-winsdk@v2](https://github.com/fbactions/setup-winsdk) to install the target version of Windows SDK, but this is not enough so we also add env variable to force SDK detection. Both env variables and cmake variable seem to be required, the former are used by DXC's `FindD3D12` script and others are for CMake's generic SDK detection.

Example of successful CI run: https://github.com/eliemichel/dawn-prebuilt/actions/runs/11861028908/job/33057504211

This is an imported pull request from
https://github.com/google/dawn/pull/23

commit.subject: Allow Requiring Higher Range Size Limits for ImmediateDataRange
commit.message:
Allow Requiring Higher Range Size Limits for ImmediateDataRange

This CL add abilities to require higher range size limits for
ImmediateDataRange.
It do below changes to achieve this:
- Split "kMaxImmediateDataByteSize" to
  "kDeviceDefaultImmediateDataBytes" and "kAdapterMaxImmediateDataBytes".
  These two constants defines the default limits for adapter and device.
- Validate the limits if it is required by user.

And this CL also fixed a bug about uploading immediate data. The bug is
due to count immediate data dirty range in a wrong way.

Bug: 366291600
Change-Id: I094beabf976158819b82dbee0583b9faf49ecfab

commit.subject: Add dry-run option to cts roll
commit.message:
Add dry-run option to cts roll

This allows you to see both the list of tests as well as the
commit message, which shows the list of pull requests that will
be included.

Note: this is useful because I tried `--test-filter "rgba8unorm"`
forgetting it's a glob. It matched nothing and generated a CL
with 0 tests which then failed. Add this option less you see
that your query/filter selected what you wanted. It also lets
you see what PRs are included which can be useful as sometimes
you want your tests to be on top of dawn's CTS version and not
github's top of tree version.

[tint] Remove uniformity function tag for subgroup matrix builtins

Only subgroupMatrixLoad could potentially have a non-uniform result,

unusable without violations.

matrix parameters to be uniform.

commit.subject: Add -test-filter option to cts roll
commit.message:
Add -test-filter option to cts roll

This lets you run a subset of the CTS on the bots via
the roller script

Example:

```
tools/run cts roll --test-filter "textureSampleLevel" --max-attempts 0 --repo https://github.com/greggman/cts.git --revision 546ab937546eb4d8af1a98d7c07ff2e6c3c0e120
```

Will run only tests with `textureSampleLevel` in their query.
`-test-filter` is a regex.

Change-Id: I4bcc8ce61cf0fd87d35799b4393ae4e68449269e

commit.subject: Move resolver based const-eval tests to the resolver folder.
commit.message:
Move resolver based const-eval tests to the resolver folder.

The const-eval tests use the resolver based testing framework. They work
by having the resolver run the const-eval. They do not call `Eval`
directly, as such they depend on the WGSL framework.

Move the tests which use the resolver into the wgsl/resolver folder. New
tests will be created in the core/constant folder which tests `Eval`
directly.

Bug: 409319601
Change-Id: I5fd6cb8f4843bec0eaf4c47b53e3350b3d0e7e9f

commit.subject: [spirv-writer] Make block emission non-recursive.
commit.message:
[spirv-writer] Make block emission non-recursive.

Change the spirv-writer to not recurse through blocks during emission.
Instead, blocks are stored into the functions and a list of blocks to
emit is maintained. We then emit from the list.

Bug: 409346479
Change-Id: Ibc6fad2ac2a4845e1ec952b62bb01dd0bce2a8c6

commit.subject: D3D11: Add an option to skip fence signal for STM's access.
commit.message:
D3D11: Add an option to skip fence signal for STM's access.

Add a new option to SharedTextureMemoryD3D11Texture2DDescriptor to skip
fence signaling when the texture is accessed in a command buffer.

This is typically used when the texture is shared between ANGLE & Dawn
which share the same D3D11 device.
It will also be useful for dcomp textures. Dcomp doesn't use the same
D3D11 device as Dawn. However it's not required to signal any fence
before returning the texture to dcomp. Dcomp still requires dawn to wait
on its own fence anw.

Bug: chromium:335003893
Change-Id: Ibf28cc5d84456f623b20f087cc23aa824e2131bd

commit.message:
[tint] Fix zero-value composite constructors with subgroup matrices

If a constructor contains a subgroup matrix then its evaluation stage
must be runtime. This prevents the resolver from trying to create
constant values with subgroup matrix types.

Fixed: 409367436

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding supressions for a
  couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding supressions for a
  couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding supressions for a
  couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for a
  couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding supressions for a
  couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for a
  couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Turns off `treat_warnings_as_errors`, since chromium doesn't support
  MSVC, thus dependencies we inherit from it have building warnings
  that are unlikely to get fixed.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Turns off `treat_warnings_as_errors` for Win MSVC builds, since
  chromium doesn't support MSVC, thus dependencies we inherit from it
  have building warnings that are unlikely to get fixed.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Turns off Tint IR binary related targets, i.e. IR Fuzzer, for Win
  MSVC builds, since chromium doesn't support MSVC, thus dependencies
  we inherit from it have building warnings that are unlikely to get
  fixed.
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.

- Turns off warnings for MSVC builds, since chromium doesn't support
  MSVC, thus dependencies we inherit from it have building warnings
  that are unlikely to get fixed.

- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil (needs various libc++ updates)
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf +
  asbeil (needs various libc++ updates)
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing is
  enabled and if ir binary is enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing and
  IR binary are both enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing and
  IR binary are both enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing and
  IR binary are both enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing and
  IR binary are both enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"
commit.message:
Reapply "[tint][ir][fuzz] Enable by default"

This reverts commit e64a1d19970ed90f44440b9a54ddcf5ec00f0326.

- Removes having a separate flag for tint_build_ir_fuzzer from
  tint_build_ir_binary
- Building IR fuzzer will now instead be controlled by if fuzzing and
  IR binary are both enabled
- Rolls protobuf and protoc_wrapper ahead to pick up fixes for issues
  that were causing build failures when using siso
- Rolls abseil ahead, because there is KIs with GCC + protobuf
- Ripped out the existing custom gn rules we had for abseil, instead
  now using the upstream ones. (This required adding suppressions for
  a couple clang extension issues in configs)
- Rolls libprotobuf-mutator ahead, since the roll to protobuf brought
  in a new point version with API changes
- Rolls testing/ since it depends on lpm, and is broken by the roll
- Added in third_party/fuzztest/src, since testing/ now depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Added in third_party/re2/src, since fuzztest depends on it,
  using the BUILD.gn from chromium
- Moves third_party/googletest to third_party/googletest/src and using
  BUILD.gn from chromium, so that fuzztest can build
- Add an ASAN suppression in script for IR corpus generation, because
  there is an ODR violation in asbeil that it failing on.
- Rolls build/, buildtools/, tools/clang, and gn ahead, since other
  DEPS rolls depend on these rolling
- Various fixes for the BUILD and CMake files

commit.subject: Dawn: Ensure pipeline creation don't use tintProgram before cache missed
commit.message:
Dawn: Ensure pipeline creation don't use tintProgram before cache missed

This CL make shader module cache all reflection information OpenGL
backend needed when creating pipeline into the entry point metadata
table, so OpenGL backend don't need to use Tint program before shader
module compilation cache missed.

With this CL, all backends will not actually use Tint program before
shader module compilation cache missed. This is one step towards cache
becoming completely independent on Tint program.

commit.subject: [spirv-writer] Store SPIR-V instructions into blocks.
commit.message:
[spirv-writer] Store SPIR-V instructions into blocks.

Currently the SPIR-V writer creates a list of instructions for a
function, those lists contain multiple SPIR-V blocks just appended
together. Instead, create a list of blocks, the blocks store
instructions. Then as blocks are emitted from the Tint IR they create
Blocks in the SPIR-V writer. This will allow us to refer to those SPIR-V
blocks later.

Bug: 409346479
Change-Id: Iaecef8f4293426af722ec45946aa1274a693864b

commit.message:
[spirv-writer] Remove label members from printer.

In the SPIR-V printer, instead of storing the label for the current
loop, if, switch merge or the loop header, instead use the
`GetMergeLabel` method for merges and add a `GetLoopHeaderLabel` to get
the header for a loop block.

Bug: 409346479
Change-Id: Ie29019e6696e43721034ffcc209befa790f50e32

commit.subject: D3D11: assign separate native binding index for each stage.
commit.message:
D3D11: assign separate native binding index for each stage.

Previously we used the same D3D binding index counter for all stages
even if some resources are not used in some stages.

For example. a BindGroup with 3 buffers:
- buffer A, visibility=Fragment
- buffer B, visibility=Vertex
- buffer C, visibility=Fragment

They would be assigned to:
- buffer A: PS slot 0.
  - VS slot 0 is skipped.
- buffer B: VS slot 1.
  - PS slot 1 is skipped.
- buffer C: PS slot 2.
  - VS slot 2 is skipped.

It resulted in:
- VS slot 0 and 2 would be wasted and wouldn't be used by any resource.
- PS slot 1 would be wasted.

This CL changes the binding indices' assignment logic such that each
stage has their own counter. Thus, the above buffers would be assigned
to:
- buffer A: PS slot 0.
- buffer B: VS slot 0.
- buffer C: PS slot 1.

This will also make the resources' stage specific indices continuous.
It makes it possible to bind all resources in one D3D call if we want
to in future.

Bug: 42240704
Change-Id: Ib70c5f32ccbbdff03212bc2b7d3cc1b76154fc9c

commit.subject: [ir][fuzz] Handle invalid workgroup sizes in fuzzer.
commit.message:
[ir][fuzz] Handle invalid workgroup sizes in fuzzer.

Then wokgroup size is checked by Dawn and Tint exe outside of the tint
backend. Add a similar check into the WGSL fuzzer so we don't fail with
a validation error.

This is not checked in the const-eval code for SubstituteOverrides
because Dawn needs the result of the const-eval to do it's own checks,
and shouldn't fail before it does so.

Bug: 408370947
Change-Id: I7ae3011c314e0d1abac068e2b34bdd95031271d5

commit.subject: D3D11: Only reset used UAV slots.
commit.message:
D3D11: Only reset used UAV slots.

Previously we reset all UAV slots from 0 to max used slot.
However UAVs are bound starting from highest index and with decreasing
indices. That means the beginning slots (from 0) might not be used at
all.

This CL adds code to keep track of min and max UAV slot. At the end of a
compute/render pass, we will only reset [min, max] UAV slots.

Bug: 42240704
Change-Id: I73049425cade43dc26923a6778cb329fc8565c41

commit.subject: D3D11: Cache SRVs and RTVs in the Texture.
commit.message:
D3D11: Cache SRVs and RTVs in the Texture.

It's a common scenario that users create a texture's view transiently
once per frame and never cache it.
e.g:
void renderStep() {
    // Create a view and attach it to a render pass.
    wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor renderPassDesc = ...;
    renderPassDesc.colorAttachments[0].view = texture.CreateView();

    // Draw the render pass.
}

In this case, D3D11 has to repeatedly re-create the texture's D3D native
view every frame. This is not a cheap operation. Unlike metal backend,
where the view creation could be skipped entirely in some simple
scenarios:
See: https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/dawn/src/dawn/native/metal/TextureMTL.mm;drc=5ca64904963dc4676216ddfd226779522c271540;l=104

This CL adds a small optimization for this scenario by:
- Caching D3D views within the wgpu::Texture object.
- Checking the cache for an existing D3D view before creating a new one
when a wgpu::TextureView is initialized.
- Implementing a view cache with a limited capacity (currently max 3
views).

Bug: chromium:377716220
Change-Id: Id99c38f8c91dc441f9a6ba92ca888dea3e8d37dc

It's a common scenario that users create a texture's view transiently
once per frame and never cache it.
e.g:
void renderStep() {
    // Create a view and attach it to a render pass.
    wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor renderPassDesc = ...;
    renderPassDesc.colorAttachments[0].view = texture.CreateView();

    // Draw the render pass.
}

In this case, D3D11 has to repeatedly re-create the texture's D3D native
view every frame. This is not a cheap operation. Unlike metal backend,
where the view creation could be skipped entirely in some simple
scenarios:
See: https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/dawn/src/dawn/native/metal/TextureMTL.mm;drc=5ca64904963dc4676216ddfd226779522c271540;l=104

This CL adds a small optimization for this scenario by:
- Caching last created D3D views within the wgpu::Texture object.
- Checking the cache for an existing D3D view before creating a new one
when a wgpu::TextureView is initialized.

Bug: chromium:377716220
Change-Id: Id99c38f8c91dc441f9a6ba92ca888dea3e8d37dc

commit.subject: [vulkan] Free recycled memory at idle
commit.message:
[vulkan] Free recycled memory at idle

In the Vulkan backend ensure that any recycled memory being held in
PooledResourceMemoryAllocator(s) for ResourceMemoryAllocator is freed
periodically. Do this from the ReduceMemoryUsage() function. This should
help reduce max allocated GPU memory in graphite/dawn/vulkan.

Bug: 407730048
Change-Id: Iee6369f0b2b2a01391fbe67bbc5eb691f419607c

commit.message:
Remove outdated expectations for copyToTexture

Some of the core issues behind this appear to have been fixed, and the
remaining failures on swiftshader seem to largely be flaky OOM issues,
as all of them that I could find indicated that they failed while
attempting to perform some operation against an invalid texture, but
which test it was that was failing would shift.

Marking the swiftshader tests as RetryOnFailure appears to allow it to
move past any transient failures, and the rest seem to be good to remove
outright.

commit.subject: Revert "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading""
commit.message:
Revert "Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading""

This reverts commit e579b628e5d5276086b6a2eaefa1718586bc7e18.

Reason for revert: Multiple bots are reporting infra issues with "The following files are missing: dxil.dll, dxcompiler.dll"

Original change's description:
> Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"
>
> This is a reland of commit e4d4669d79501b1acdd2bf017ba491b611d741da
>
> Remove build_with_chromium statements in test GN files that copy
> DLLs. Rely on copies instructions which already exist with the D3D12
> files.
>
> To appease Skia builds which do not depend on the Windows SDK,
> fallback to system FXC if the local directory version is not found.
>
> Original change's description:
> > Improve DX compiler library loading
> >
> > Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.
> > D3D12 compiler DLLs were further sourced from the local user's SDK
> > directory as a fallback.
> >
> > For better security, load DX compiler DLLs using full paths, with
> > SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS for better security. Scenarios
> > such as Skia and x86 builds where we need dawn_use_built_dxc will
> > fallback to FXC. No fallbacks to local user SDK directories.
> >
> > Bug:356665092
> > Change-Id: Ib4148f9b89da694e3868b4f3c3c329a4b06ce922
> > Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/229754
> > Reviewed-by: Corentin Wallez <cwallez@chromium.org>
> > Commit-Queue: Rafael Cintron <rafael.cintron@microsoft.com>
> > Reviewed-by: Antonio Maiorano <amaiorano@google.com>
>
> Bug: 356665092
> Change-Id: Ic05d20c47c5db3021f9e38b724bf527bfba52a5e
> Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/233216

commit.subject: Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"
commit.message:
Reland "Improve DX compiler library loading"

This is a reland of commit e4d4669d79501b1acdd2bf017ba491b611d741da

Original change's description:
> Improve DX compiler library loading
>
> Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.
> D3D12 compiler DLLs were further sourced from the local user's SDK
> directory as a fallback.
>
> For better security, load DX compiler DLLs using full paths, with
> SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS for better security. Scenarios
> such as Skia and x86 builds where we need dawn_use_built_dxc will
> fallback to FXC. No fallbacks to local user SDK directories.
>
> Bug:356665092
> Change-Id: Ib4148f9b89da694e3868b4f3c3c329a4b06ce922

commit.subject: [tint][wgsl] Add `__constructible` to intrinsics def
commit.message:
[tint][wgsl] Add `__constructible` to intrinsics def

This allows us to express the restriction that a type must be
constructible, which is the case for workgroupUniformLoad(). We can
then remove the special-case validation from the resolver.

Special-case the test permutation logic to expand __constructible to a
list of actual types.

Fixed: 408195607
Change-Id: Ic2b020e6fb243b0638a9225c1c2c01689bcf5940

commit.subject: D3D11: avoid redundant binding settings
commit.message:
D3D11: avoid redundant binding settings

Currently BindGroupTrackerD3D11 does a lot of redundant bindings.
In destructor it also attempts to reset all available binding slots:
- 14x2 constant buffer slots.
- 128x2 shader resource slots.
- 16x2 sampler slots.
- 64 UAV slots.
Even if not all binding slots are used during a compute/render pass.

This CL prevents redundant bindings from happening. This is important
because each D3D API call has overheads. Especially when the D3D11
device context has internal multithreading protection's overheads.

This is achieved by tracking current bound resources and avoid calling
D3D11 binding API if the binding is unchanged. The current max bound
slot will also be tracked to reset minimal set of slots in dtor instead
of resetting everything.

Bug: 42240704
Change-Id: I7d4ec2d4dbfc0ab9d69d4553159c17897aa4bf30

commit.subject: cts roller: don't retrigger builds that already have results
commit.message:
cts roller: don't retrigger builds that already have results

Previously GetOrStartBuildsAndWait would only check the status of the
most recent build on each builder, retriggering it if it finished but
didn't produce results (Unknown, InfraFailure, Canceled).

Prioritize Success/Failure builds over those so we don't rerun just
because there was a more recent canceled build. This should allow
running `tools/run cts update-expectations` more robustly against
existing CLs (like failed autoroll jobs).

TODO: haven't been able to test this yet because I don't seem to have
resultdb access for some reason.

Bug: none

commit.subject: Reland "Range Analysis: Get loop exit condition from body block"
commit.message:
Reland "Range Analysis: Get loop exit condition from body block"

This is a reland of commit 1411699ba4cdf29eca037c4320543ab8189bad28

Original change's description:
> Range Analysis: Get loop exit condition from body block
>
> This patch is the third part to implement the computation of the
> range on the loop control variables. In this patch we implement the
> function `GetBinaryToCompareLoopControlVariableInLoopBody()` to get
> the condition to exit the loop in the loop body block if the loop
> meets the below requirements (a straightforward for-loop):
> - The loop control variable is only used as the parameter of the
>   load instruction.
> - The first instruction is to load the loop control variable into a
>   temporary variable.
> - The second instruction is to compare the temporary variable with
>   a constant value and save the result to a boolean variable.
> - The second instruction cannot be a comparison that will never be
>   true (out of range of 32-bit integer).
> - The third instruction is an `ifelse` expression that uses the
>   boolean variable got in the second instruction as the condition.
> - The true block of the above `ifelse` expression doesn't contain
>   `exit_loop`.
> - The false block of the above `ifelse` expression only contains
>   `exit_loop`.
>
> Bug: chromium:348701956
> Test: tint_unittests
> Change-Id: Ie99911791eb6530e6d081ac9b54c2ec74e1be64c
> Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/233294
> Commit-Queue: Jiawei Shao <jiawei.shao@intel.com>
> Reviewed-by: James Price <jrprice@google.com>

commit.subject: test_runner.js: fix heartbeat code disrupting async behavior
commit.message:
test_runner.js: fix heartbeat code disrupting async behavior

The way we injected heartbeats meant we were returning a userspace
promise to the CTS, rather than the real one from the browser.
Modify this so that we attach heartbeats to the promise, but still
return the original promise object. This fixes
`webgpu:api,validation,buffer,mapping:` tests that were testing the
exact behavior of the API (task vs. microtask).

There's a small chance this will fix some other tests, too.

I've also fixed the code that was supposed to trigger a heartbeat both
before and after the responding code, which I'm pretty sure would not
have worked: resolve() does not run the awaiting code, it just marks the
promise as resolved, so both heartbeats ran before. I don't think this
is important, but it shouldn't hurt anything to have more heartbeats.

Fixed: 42241427
Change-Id: I4995c3518f1dc5d05524a0155f601f9103891d8d

commit.subject: Convert --test-launcher-summary-output
commit.message:
Convert --test-launcher-summary-output

Makes the necessary changes to automatically convert the
--test-launcher-summary-output= argument for tests to
--gtest_output=json: in standalone Dawn checkouts.

The former is passed in when running in a Chromium checkout in order
to output results to a known location for consumption by ResultDB.
However, it is a Chromium-specific argument handled by "base", which
is not usable in Dawn.

--gtest_output is built into gtest and functions similarly, although
its output format is different.

This change is necessary in order to have Dawn standalone builders
whose tests are compatible with ResultDB.

Bug: 385317083
Change-Id: I69e23dca4afa7a1e6da73953835b089755a7db96

commit.message:
[ir] Add SetResult() setter for single-result instructions

Most instructions only have a single result, so this overload removes
the need to construct and iterate over a vector that only has a single
element most of the time.

commit.subject: [ir] Add Result() getter for single-result instructions
commit.message:
[ir] Add Result() getter for single-result instructions

The vast majority of instructions only have a single result. Most
callsites of the existing `Result` method just call `Result(0)`.

The helper removes the need to pass `0`, and also asserts that there
is indeed exactly one result. This would help catch places where we
may wrongfully assume there is only a single result.

Bug: 372671446
Change-Id: I0fdbe3316e1e63abbadf5828d743f9bd737ca4f4

commit.subject: Range Analysis: Get loop exit condition from body block
commit.message:
Range Analysis: Get loop exit condition from body block

This patch is the third part to implement the computation of the
range on the loop control variables. In this patch we implement the
function `GetBinaryToCompareLoopControlVariableInLoopBody()` to get
the condition to exit the loop in the loop body block if the loop
meets the below requirements (a straightforward for-loop):
- The loop control variable is only used as the parameter of the
  load instruction.
- The first instruction is to load the loop control variable into a
  temporary variable.
- The second instruction is to compare the temporary variable with
  a constant value and save the result to a boolean variable.
- The third instruction is an `ifelse` expression that uses the
  boolean variable got in the second instruction as the condition.
- The true block of the above `ifelse` expression doesn't contain
  `exit_loop`.
- The false block of the above `ifelse` expression only contains
  `exit_loop`.

Bug: chromium:348701956
Test: tint_unittests
Change-Id: Ie99911791eb6530e6d081ac9b54c2ec74e1be64c

commit.subject: D3D11: Enable storage buffers in VS for feature level 11.0
commit.message:
D3D11: Enable storage buffers in VS for feature level 11.0

Feature level 11.0 doesn't have UAVs in VS. UAVs are used for
implementing writable storage buffers. However, Dawn/WebGPU spec only
allows read-only storage buffers in VS, so it's safe to advertise that
storage buffers are available in VS. Read-only storage buffers will be
implemented by SRVs which all stages have.

Bug: 388028942
Change-Id: Ib78b3bd5ac5bb3cec325879a9c1bbbffd9dfb95c

commit.subject: [intrinsics] Allow setting the namespace for enums.
commit.message:
[intrinsics] Allow setting the namespace for enums.

Add an attribute `@ns()` to the `enum` entry in the intrinsics file.
This allows setting the namespace used in the matchers for the enum, so
you can provide something like `@ns("spirv::type")` to change from
`core::` to `spirv::type::` in the generated matcher code. The default
value is `core`.

commit.subject: Compat: unlower limits
commit.message:
Compat: unlower limits

Because we excluded Mali-T624,T628,T720 we can make the
lower limit of maxStorageBuffersPerShaderStage be 8,
maxStorageBuffersInFragmentShaders be 4,
and maxStorageTexturesInFragmentShaders be 4

I removed 2 tests because AFAICT they are hard to fix AND, they
are tested in the CTS so they'll still be tested.

The issue is the tests were testing that, in compat, when
maxStorageTexturesInFragmentStage is less than
maxStorageTexturesPerFragmentStage and you try to use
more than maxStorageTexturesInFragmentStage you get an
error. This only happens in compat because in core the
2 limits are always the max of the 2.

With the change so that maxStorageTextureInFragmentStage
is 4 it's not, by default, lower than maxStorageTexturesPerShaderStage
which is also 4.

The testing infra for the dawn_unittests doesn't appear to
have any easy way to change this. To test you'd need some way
to tell dawn to return an adapter with maxStorageTexturesPerShaderStage
greater than 4. Setting that all up seems like a waste of time given
the CTS can and does test this already.

If it is important it can be done in a different CL.

Note: tested this with a CTS that expects the new limits.
Note: this will have to wait for a CTS roll or suppressions
added to expectations.

Bug: 406729256,406729255
Fixed: 406729256,406729255
Change-Id: I9c1ddbba8d1a9e65a899ef978e3b214ae6affd28

commit.subject: [tools][cts] Fix roller interaction with new globs
commit.message:
[tools][cts] Fix roller interaction with new globs

Updates the CTS roller to properly handle the new glob style, which
allows for any number of * wildcards throughout the expectation.
Previously, only a single un-escaped wildcard was allowed at the very
end.

The new code does not distinguish between the old and new approaches
in the expectation files (set via "# full_wildcard_support: true"), as
the new approach is backwards compatible with older style expectations,
albeit less efficient during comparisons. We do not expect to ever move
back to the older style, so the reduced complexity is worth the small
efficiency hit in the off-chance we need to go back temporarily for
some reason.

Bug: 406978213
Change-Id: If678457ed80d2d73e8c416be11efdde78103e05e

commit.message:
Add block-all-features flag to run-cts

This gets passed to the CTS which, as it says, blocks-all-features.

commit.subject: [tint][inspector] Unify texture builtin handling.
commit.message:
[tint][inspector] Unify texture builtin handling.

Many pieces of metadata about textures and samplers were gathered that
depend on a combination of the texture, the sampler and the builtin that
are used. Because handles can be passed by argument to functions, the
gathering needs to trace which handles are passed around by function
call. There were three different ways to do this and this CL unifies
them into single one. The logic of what to do with the builtin call is
also grouped in one place.

This will help support binding_array for these queries since it will
need to be handled in only one place.

The return type of SamplerTexturePairs is changed from VectorRef to
std::vector to avoid leaking the type in users of Tint.

Logic to track TextureSamplerPairs is no longer used and removed from
the resolver

commit.subject: CTS expectations: file many bugs, other maintenance
commit.message:
CTS expectations: file many bugs, other maintenance

- Replace all links with post-migration buganizer IDs
- Strictly separate Skips from everything else, clean up some confusing
  old leftover headers
- Attempt to manually cluster bugs, primarily those that didn't have bug
  IDs, but also some that did because they overlapped
  - Unlink some bugs that are linked incorrectly because of bug 42241471
    (but only the ones I happened upon)
  - Removed a number of expectation tags that _probably_ weren't
    relevant in order to simplify expectations overall
- Move most expectations out of the "please triage" sections
- File bugs for everything that's not in the "please triage" sections

Theoretically I tried not to lift any expectations, but there's a good
chance I made some small mistakes. If they show up in FYI hopefully
they're not too annoying to fix.

commit.subject: [tint][uniformity] Fix loop-in data flow edges
commit.message:
[tint][uniformity] Fix loop-in data flow edges

Edges were only being propagated when the behavior of the loop body
contained `next`. We also need to propagate from the loop-continuing
block when the body behavior was just `continue`.

Fix this by moving the logic for propagating values to loop-in nodes
next to the loop-continuing handling code, so that we do not rely on
values being propagated up the variable scope stack.

Fixed: 405600543
Change-Id: I897cabdb1ba4a21e765d669fde9240e2343a1f2b

commit.message:
[tint][uniformity] Fix data flow for continue statements

Loop continuing blocks need extra nodes to combine data flow paths
from each continue statement that branches to them, otherwise we only
see the value that was present at the end of the loop body.

commit.subject: Use OutputName for tint "test" target names
commit.message:
Use OutputName for tint "test" target names

Makes the following changes related to tint "test" GN targets:

1. Makes them use OutputName instead of "test_cmd"/"bench_cmd" for the
   target name. Having an output name from the target name causes issues
   when attempting to run tests on Swarming.
2. Adds a check to the generator Go code to ensure that all targets of
   those types have OutputName set.
3. Updates the non-generated references to "test_cmd"/"bench_cmd"
   targets.

This should hopefully be a no-op as far as users and automation is
concerned.

Change-Id: I40b95a9afdeb0ffd4dc2f2d36b66e7cb57019d09

Makes the following changes related to tint "test" GN targets defined
by the test_cmd target type during generation:

1. Makes them use OutputName instead of "test_cmd" for the target name.
   Having an output name from the target name causes issues when
   attempting to run tests on Swarming.

   those types have OutputName set.

   targets.

This should hopefully be a no-op as far as users and automation is
concerned.

This could be applied to "bench_cmd" types as well, but is not currently
necessary and will require some additional work due to an existing
Chrome dependency on the current name.

commit.subject: [BitSet] Add/update bit search and count methods
commit.message:
[BitSet] Add/update bit search and count methods

Part of a larger set of changes to update Dawn's BitSet implementation.

Adds BitCount and ScanReverse, updates ScanForward. All methods have
explicit implementations for 8, 16, 32, and 64 bit.

Implementations are taken from ANGLE's mathutil.h
